next_step: Closed — procurement pushed back due to firmwide air-gap mandate. Re-engage if policy changes.
notes:
Summary: Enclave is a defense-focused provider building an end-user assistant for classified operational docs. They require a fully air-gapped on-prem deployment with no outbound control-plane connectivity; legal and cybersecurity teams will not sign off on any managed control plane. We scoped Redwood Private (on-prem bundle) but the customer's security team stated it still requires a vendor-free air gap.

Key quote: "We cannot allow any persistent egress to a vendor control plane — everything must live inside our enclave/DMZ with FIPS-certified HSMs." — CISO (2025-11-12).

POC timeline & activities (short):
- 2025-09-10: Intro demo (Maya) — technical leadership showed interest in batching + KV cache to keep latency under 200ms.
- 2025-09-24: NDA signed; SE kickoff with Diego.
- 2025-10-05: Security questionnaire v1 submitted; asked for SOC2 and deployment architecture.
- 2025-10-28: Internal architecture call — Enclave declared need for fully air-gapped with internal control plane.
- 2025-11-12: Fireflies call (ff_2025-11-12_Enclave_POC_Call_93f4) — CISO rejected managed-control-plane approach.
- 2025-11-18: Short POC (local VM-based) to demo model correctness and latency; results shared (/drive/Redwood/Enclave/POC_Results_2025-11-18.xlsx).
- 2025-12-02: Procurement told AE that budget is frozen pending enterprise-wide compliance review.
- 2026-01-28: Last outreach — no champion identified after org reorg; competitor (Hugging Face) selected for full on-prem deliverable.

Technical requirements and notes:
- Must run inside air-gapped DMZ with HSM-backed key management (FIPS/KMS).
- Network egress = 0 policy; no telemetry to vendor endpoints.
- Required on-prem installer or appliance with customer-run control plane.
- Latency SLO: 95p < 250ms for chat flows (short prompts); throughput target ~60 concurrent requests.

Sales notes / why we lost:
- Redwood Private offered most capability, but our control-plane-dependent features (automatic rollout, cloud-based tracing, support access) conflicted with their no-egress policy.
- Customer prioritized a vendor-neutral, fully internal deployment and selected a competitor who delivered an installer they could run entirely offline.
- Internal champion left in December during engineering reorg; procurement deprioritized.

Next actions (internal):
- Mark closed-lost; add to account watchlist for policy changes.
- Keep security FAQ updated with an explicit runbook describing minimum egress options and HSM integrations so we can re-evaluate fit for similar accounts.
- Opportunity to upsell if competitor's offline solution shows quality/regression problems.

Stale outreach snippets: "We hear you — if policy changes and you can allow an audited, vendor-controlled telemetry channel, we'd re-open the private deployment conversation."

Contact list: CEO (Ari Mercer), CTO (Nadia Solanki), CISO (Tomás Rey), Head of Infra (Varun Iyer).
